text: Afterward Moses and Aaron went to Pharaoh and said, "This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: Let my people go, so they may hold a festival for me in the wilderness."
But Pharaoh said, "Who is the LORD, that I should obey his voice and let Israel go? I do not know the LORD, and I will not let Israel go."
Then they said, "The God of the Hebrews has met with us. Let us go three days' journey into the wilderness to sacrifice to the LORD our God, or he may strike us with plague or with the sword."
But the king of Egypt said to them, "Moses and Aaron, why are you pulling the people away from their work? Get back to your labor!"
And Pharaoh said, "Look how numerous the people of the land are now, and you would have them stop their labor!"
That same day Pharaoh gave orders to the slave drivers over the people and to their foremen:
"You shall no longer supply the people with straw for making bricks, as you did before. Let them go and gather their own straw.
But require of them the same quota of bricks they made before; do not reduce it. They are lazy—that is why they cry out, 'Let us go and sacrifice to our God.'
Make the work heavier for these men, so they keep at it and pay no attention to lying words."
So the slave drivers and the foremen went out and said to the people, "This is what Pharaoh says: I will no longer give you straw.
Go and get your own straw wherever you can find it—but your workload will not be reduced in the least."

versions.text: Go and get your own straw wherever you can find it—but your workload will not be reduced by a single brick."
versions.explanation: The Hebrew says "nothing at all shall be reduced from your work"; "by a single brick" imports a detail not in the text (bricks are mentioned later, in v. 19). "In the least" keeps the force without adding content.

text: So the people scattered throughout the whole land of Egypt to gather stubble for straw.
The slave drivers kept pressing them: "Finish your work—the same daily quota as when the straw was provided."

And the foremen of the Israelites, whom Pharaoh's slave drivers had appointed over them, were beaten, and they were asked, "Why did you not complete your required quota of bricks yesterday or today, as you did before?"

versions.text: And the foremen of the Israelites, whom Pharaoh's slave drivers had appointed over them, were beaten and asked, "Why haven't you met your quota of bricks yesterday or today, as you did before?"
versions.explanation: As written, "were beaten and asked" reads as though the foremen themselves asked the question; in Hebrew the taskmasters beat them and put the question to them. Adding "and they were asked" keeps the passive parallel clear when read aloud.

versions.text: And the foremen of the Israelites, whom Pharaoh's slave drivers had appointed over them, were beaten, and they were asked, "Why have you not finished your required quota of bricks yesterday or today, as you did before?"
versions.explanation: The present perfect ("have you not finished") does not combine with the past time marker "yesterday" in standard English; the simple past ("did you not complete") is grammatical and reads more cleanly aloud while preserving the Hebrew sense of the unfinished prescribed brick quota.

text: Then the Israelite foremen went to Pharaoh and cried out, "Why do you treat your servants this way?
No straw is given to your servants, yet they tell us, 'Make bricks!' Your servants are being beaten, but the fault lies with your own people."
But he said, "Lazy—that's what you are, lazy! That is why you say, 'Let us go and sacrifice to the LORD.'
Now get to work! You will be given no straw, yet you must deliver the full number of bricks."
The Israelite foremen saw that they were in trouble when they were told, "You must not reduce the daily number of bricks."
When they left Pharaoh, they came upon Moses and Aaron, who stood waiting for them,
and they said to them, "May the LORD look upon you and judge you! You have made us a stench to Pharaoh and his officials—you have put a sword in their hand to kill us."
Then Moses turned to the LORD and said, "Lord, why have you brought harm on this people? Why did you ever send me?
Ever since I went to Pharaoh to speak in your name, he has brought harm on this people, and you have done nothing at all to rescue your people."
